name: Momentum Rotation
rationale: Momentum-rotation rules rank multiple assets by recent relative strength and allocate to the strongest assets.
expected_benefit: Potential diversification and better participation in leadership trends than a single-asset strategy.
failure_modes: Overfitting ranking windows and rebalance schedules.
Misleading results if cross-asset calendars, dividends, or benchmark alignment are inconsistent.

canonical_variants.name: Top-N relative strength rotation
canonical_variants.description: Rank assets by trailing return and hold the top N assets until the next rebalance date.
canonical_variants.hypothesis_template: A monthly top-N relative-strength rotation may improve risk-adjusted return versus a static benchmark portfolio without excessive turnover.
canonical_variants.minimum_acceptable_performance: Improve Sharpe versus a prespecified static benchmark while keeping turnover and drawdown within predefined limits.

suggested_validation: Define the asset universe before seeing results.
Define ranking lookback, rebalance frequency, and top-N count before running.
Use walk-forward validation and avoid broad parameter sweeps.
Audit calendar alignment and missing data handling before trusting results.
references: Jegadeesh and Titman, Returns to Buying Winners and Selling Losers
Faber, A Quantitative Approach to Tactical Asset Allocation
execution_notes: The current portfolio engine supports static weights, but not dynamic cross-sectional ranking or scheduled rotation.
